A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSNR work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A1-A15 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments in Section 5 and Tables 1-2, with additional ablations, generalization tests, and computational measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original reconstruction experiments and appendix analyses, including quantitative comparisons, convergence curves, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The null-restricted Laplacian, spectral subspace selection, learned predictor, reconstruction objective, and solver integrations are retained. Renaming regularization parameters to eta does not change the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain compressed sensing, super-resolution, demosaicing, and deblurring with the same dataset coverage, including CIFAR-10, CelebA, Places365, SAR, and DIV2K. Appendix distribution-shift and operator-mismatch scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PnP, NPN, DDN-Cascade, DDN-Independent, NSN, and Unrolling. The diffusion, denoiser, and appendix comparisons likewise retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5 and the appendices retain the same data settings, metrics, noise level, training budget, and iteration limits. Tables 3 and 5 rename parameters without changing their numerical settings.

E4.justification: The graph-choice, subspace-dimension, regularizer, and convergence analyses remain, as do the architecture and cross-dataset tests in A14 and operator-mismatch test in A15. Restyled or relocated plots present existing analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings are retained. For example, Table 1 keeps GSNR-PnP with L4nn at 29.42 dB for super-resolution and 39.89 dB for demosaicing; Table 7 retains 33.69 and 33.65 dB. Figure restyling does not introduce new reported results.

T1.justification: Theorems 1-2, Proposition 1, and their proofs in A1-A3 are unchanged. Mathematical edits concern notation and typesetting rather than definitions, assumptions, or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about graph-smooth null-space representation, coverage, predictability, convergence, and solver compatibility, including the stated performance improvements.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reconstruction quality and convergence are retained. The limitations concerning eigendecomposition cost, sensing-operator knowledge, and nonlinear inverse problems remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The network and optimizer description, implicit Laplacian and ARPACK implementation in A5, computational costs in A13, and code-access information are retained. Parameter renaming adds no implementation information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged. Reference edits update bibliographic metadata, including the year of reference 12 and the title of reference 44, without establishing added or removed prior work.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes prior and denoiser parameter notation to eta, updates iteration notation and the diffusion-step symbol, adds acknowledgements, corrects an author-name accent, and revises bibliography entries. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 8 rearranges and recolors panels and curves; Figure 22 changes method-header and best-score styling. Several plot labels are updated, Table 2 highlights both tied-best rows, and appendix figures and tables reflow. The same displays and evidence are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through consistent parameter notation across objectives, algorithms, and settings tables, clearer visual correspondence in Figure 8, and corrected tied-best highlighting in Table 2. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, limiting the overall gain to presentation and consistency.
